set.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. The Razorback is a small cragging spot between the Southeast Buttress and the East Tower: hike up and right of the buttress to just below the tower, with the lines on the formation's right-hand side as seen when walking up. Razorbutt is a wide crack on the formation's rear face; climb the slope and curl behind the rock to find it.

review.notes: Approach from Mount Prindle and Razorback pages; start from route Location. The route page only says it is used to set up top ropes, so no descent.

set.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. The Southeast Buttress is the feature on the right side of the main wall. Hike up and swing right round the buttress, past the small formation called Razorback; the first pitch begins just above it.
set.descent_text: After the last pitch, untie, walk to the true summit, and descend to the right into the amphitheatre; it returns you to the base of the climb.

review.notes: Approach from Prindle and buttress pages and route Location; descent from the route page only.

set.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. The Southeast Buttress is the feature on the right side of the main wall. Homewrecker takes the prominent dihedral that arcs leftward near the middle of the buttress; the first pitch starts up a low-angle grassy gully at the middle of the buttress toe, which most parties scramble.
set.descent_text: From the anchor behind the summit tower, rappel into the gully. Downclimb fourth-class ground to a big boulder with slings beneath it, then rappel again to the floor of the Keyhole.

review.notes: Approach from Prindle and buttress pages and route Location; descent from the route page only (rope length and rappel counts omitted).

set.approach: From Palmer, take North Palmer Fishhook Road to the Mother Lode Lodge switchback, then the gravel Archangel Road, and follow it past the bridge to the Reed Lakes trailhead. The trail winds up to an abandoned cabin, where the climbing and bouldering in the basin begins. Spirit Boulder Area lies left of the approach gully that serves Shield, Main Wall and Two Toke Tower, and Cali Slit is left of the Spirit Boulder chalice. It slabs past two bolts into a roof, then crosses the lip into a left-trending slit.

review.notes: Approach from Reed Lakes and Spirit Boulder pages; start from route text. Anchor noted but no descent stated.

set.approach: Little Switzerland on the Pika Glacier in Denali National Park is reached by air taxi from Talkeetna, and the approach from Pika base camp to The Throne is very short. The route climbs the formation's west face, just left of a roof coated in vivid green lichen, starting off snow onto an easy unprotected face leading to a moderate crack system and a large ledge, before merging into the northwest ridge near the formation's midpoint. It begins left of Swisser than Swiss Chocolate and right of the popular single-pitch cragging cracks.
set.descent_text: From the west summit, go down The Lost Marsupial route on the formation's south side to reach the glacier.

review.notes: Approach from Little Switzerland and Throne pages; start and descent from the route page.

set.approach: Heading out from Haines, park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch and follow the creek past the culvert to a flagged trail into the woods, which leads to a boulder field. A trail runs up the right side of the boulder field to the main wall, arriving at the base of Chest Fur, with the routes lying to its right. Dancing in Your XtraTufs is the farthest-right route on the Weird Alaska wall; it begins by clipping a bolt and moving left on exposed ground to a ledge.

review.notes: Approach from 17 Mile and Weird Alaska Wall pages; start from route text. Only a two-bolt anchor with rings is mentioned, so no descent.
